The full subcategory of Top of these, kHaus, is a very nice category of spaces — better-behaved in many ways than Top itself. Anyhow, the ordinary topological product of two k-spaces may not itself be a k-space; but it has an associated space (sometimes called its “k-ification”) which, while not a product in Top, is a product in kHaus. The more elementary example is with coproducts not products, but sticking “op” on the categories involved makes it an example with products.
